Subject: MSA + Order Form — indemnity redlines (Royale Tech)

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward but legal flagged several items in the MSA and Order Form related to IP and indemnity. I've attached a redline (Royale_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf) with the changes we'll need to see before procurement signs off. High-level concerns:

- Vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims tied to the delivered software and model outputs; we want Redwood to defend and indemnify against infringement claims that arise from the model/service.
- Exclusions: we proposed carveouts for open-source components, customer-provided data/prompts, and downstream customer modifications.
- Insurance minimums and a requirement for evidence of coverage (certificate) on execution.
- Notice and control of defense: 30-day notice, Redwood to assume defense but we want approval rights for counsel in certain circumstances.
- Cap: we ask to tie the cap to the annualized Order Form value; please propose a fair cap if you cannot accept ours.

Can you confirm who at Redwood will handle this and whether you can provide a counter-redline? We'd like to keep this moving — target signing by the end of next week if possible.

Attachments: Royale_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (pdf - 2 pages)

Thanks,

Subject: Redwood proposed compromise language — indemnity & IP (attached counter-redline)

Hi Melissa / Rajiv,

Thanks for the clear redlines. We've reviewed and propose the following compromise terms (see attached Redwood_counterredline_20251111.pdf for inline edits):

- Scope of Redwood indemnity: Redwood will defend and indemnify Royale Tech from third-party claims alleging direct infringement of third-party intellectual property rights that are caused by (i) Redwood's proprietary software as delivered and (ii) Redwood-provided, pre-trained model weights.

- Explicit exclusions: Redwood's indemnity will not apply to claims arising from (a) open-source components used pursuant to their licenses, (b) customer-uploaded data or prompts, (c) modifications made by Royale or its downstream customers, or (d) combinations of the service with third-party products not supplied or recommended by Redwood.

- Liability cap: For covered IP indemnity, Redwood requests a liability cap equal to the total fees paid for the Service under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim. If Royale requires a higher cap, please state the requested multiple and commercial rationale.

- Defense mechanics: Royale must provide notice of claim within 30 days. Redwood will have the right to assume defense with counsel of its choice; Royale may propose substitute counsel at its expense where a material conflict exists. Redwood will not settle any claim that admits liability or imposes an obligation on Royale without Royale's written consent (not unreasonably withheld).

- Insurance and evidence: Redwood will maintain commercial general liability and professional liability/tech E&O coverage. We will provide a certificate of insurance on execution and notify Royale of material changes.

We'll also redline a short carveout for model outputs where the alleged infringement is traceable solely to customer prompts or customer data — that remains in Royale's responsibility.

Please review and let us know any non-starters. If this is acceptable in principle, we can produce a clean order form with the negotiated cap and send it via DocuSign for signatures.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Redwood proposed compromise language — indemnity & IP (attached counter-redline)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the thoughtful counter. After internal review, Royale is prepared to accept Redwood's proposed carveouts for customer data, prompts, and open-source components. We also agree to the 12-month fees cap for IP indemnity, subject to the following additions:

- Explicit coverage for third-party claims alleging that a Redwood-delivered model or component (not stemming from customer-provided prompts/data) infringes a third party's copyright or patent.
- A requirement that Redwood maintain $5M E&O/Tech liability coverage (certificate delivered on execution).
- A mutual cooperation provision where Royale may participate in the defense and approve settlements that would materially affect Royale's business or IP.

If Redwood can confirm the cap calculation as 12 months of actual paid fees under the Order Form and provide the insurance certificate, Royale can proceed to sign. We'll accept a DocuSign envelope for the final MSA + Order Form if it contains the agreed language; target to execute by Friday EOD.

Please send the final DocuSign link when ready.

Best,
Melissa
